parts: My CI test passes locally but fails on the runner about 1 in 5 times. It calls `Date.now()` and asserts the formatted date. Any ideas?

Classic timezone flake. `Date.now()` is fine — the formatter is using the machine's local timezone, which differs between your laptop and the runner.

Fix it by pinning the timezone:

```javascript
const fmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: 'UTC' });
```

Or pass `timeZone: 'UTC'` into `toLocaleString`. Either way the assertion becomes deterministic.

**Why 1 in 5?** The runner's TZ may vary per shard — you can verify with `console.log(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone)`.

Read more: [Intl docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl)
That was it — pinning UTC fixed it. Thanks!
Give me a 7-day plan to start a sourdough starter from scratch.

**Day 1:** Mix 60g whole-wheat flour + 60g water in a jar. Cover loosely, leave at room temp.

**Day 2:** Rest — nothing to do.

**Days 3–7:** Discard half, feed 60g flour + 60g water daily.

It's ready when it doubles within ~6 hours of feeding and smells pleasantly sour.
